subject: Unexpected August usage spike and VAT treatment for QuickScale
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@quickscale.io>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai, sales@redwood.ai
Cc: billing@quickscale.io
Date: 2026-09-09T08:12:00Z
Subject: Sudden August bill spike + VAT question (invoice attached)

Hi Sofia / Redwood team,

We just received the August invoice (attached) and it’s ~€18k higher than our June/July average. QuickScale didn’t change volume intentionally — we didn’t roll out any new features that would meaningfully increase token usage. The invoice also shows 20% VAT charged. As an EU VAT-registered company (IE VAT: IE1234567V), we normally use reverse charge; we thought Redwood applies reverse charge for EU B2B.

Can you: 1) provide the raw usage export for August (per-session/per-route if possible), 2) explain the spike (we see many small duplicate embedding calls in our app), and 3) confirm whether VAT should be reversed on your side or if we need a corrected invoice?

Attaching: invoice_2026-08-31.pdf, small screenshot of spikes.png

Oliver
Billing Ops 
QuickScale
oliver.grant@quickscale.io
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@quickscale.io>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-09T12:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden August bill spike + VAT question (invoice attached)

Hi Oliver — thanks for flagging this. I’m looping in Sean from Billing and Marissa from Accounts so we can get you a fast turnaround.

Short answers up front: we’ll export the per-route/per-session usage for August and investigate anomalous patterns; we’ll also check your account VAT settings and whether reverse-charge should have been applied. If an invoice correction is needed we’ll issue one and propose a provisional credit while we complete the audit.

Next steps:
- Sean will pull the detailed usage export (CSV) and an initial analysis of token distribution by endpoint.
- Marissa will validate the VAT registration handling and confirm what documentation we need from QuickScale.
- I’ll track the ticket and propose an interim credit if the spike looks like a platform-side or duplicate-calling issue.

Can you confirm your VAT number and legal entity name (as you’d like it on corrected docs)? Also, if you can share a short sample of the client-side logs showing the duplicate calls (or allow us to pull traces) that would speed root cause.

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@quickscale.io>, sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-10T09:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden August bill spike + VAT question (invoice attached)

Hi Oliver — I pulled the August usage export and ran a quick pass. Attached: usage_export_quickscale_aug2026.csv and a short summary. Highlights: 

- Total billed tokens (Aug): 12,430,218 — ~160% higher than July (4,775,103).
- 68% of the incremental tokens are concentrated in calls to /v1/embed and a custom search route (/routes/emb-index). Timestamp clustering shows multiple near-duplicate calls from a small set of session_ids between 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-14.
- Root cause hypothesis: a client-side retry loop combined with our SDK's backoff led to duplicate embedding requests on a low-latency route. We can provide the specific request IDs for you to cross-check.

What we’re proposing:
1) Provisional credit: €4,500 while we confirm that the duplicates are not legitimate usage (we recommend you scan the session_ids — I’ve highlighted the top 20 in the CSV).
2) VAT: we see no VAT ID on file for QuickScale in your account. If you provide your EU VAT number and a registration confirmation, we will reissue the invoice with reverse charge (zero-rated VAT on our side) and a corrected total.

Attachments: usage_export_quickscale_aug2026.csv, provisional_credit_note_20260910.pdf

If you confirm the VAT ID and that the highlighted requests are duplicates, I’ll apply the provisional credit and get a corrected invoice out today/tomorrow.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you prefer to walk through the CSV.

—Sean
Billing Analyst, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@quickscale.io>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: QuickScale Billing <billing@quickscale.io>
Date: 2026-09-10T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden August bill spike + VAT question (invoice attached)

Thanks Sean and Sofia — that analysis looks sensible. We dug into our logs and can confirm the client retry bug produced duplicate embedding calls on the dates you highlighted. I’ve attached our VAT registration extract and confirm our legal name should be QuickScale Ltd (VAT: IE1234567V).

Please go ahead with the provisional credit and reissue the invoice with reverse charge. For bookkeeping we’ll need:
- Corrected invoice PDF with reverse-charge note and the same invoice number + correction tag
- Credit note (PDF) showing €4,500 provisional credit applied
- Confirmation email that future B2B EU invoices from Redwood will be issued net of VAT (reverse charge) once VAT ID is recorded on your side

If you need a signed amendment, we can sign a short DocuSign for the billing terms, but it shouldn’t be necessary.

Oliver
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@quickscale.io>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-10T15:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden August bill spike + VAT question (invoice attached)

Oliver — thanks for the VAT docs and confirmation. Actions we’ve taken and next steps: 

- Applied provisional credit of €4,500 to your account (see provisional_credit_note_20260910.pdf attached). This will appear as a negative line on your next statement while we finalize the correction.
- Issued corrected invoice (corrected_invoice_20260910.pdf) with reverse-charge language and your VAT number on file. The corrected invoice replaces the VAT lines and updates the net total; the invoice number is the original with a "+CORR1" suffix.
- We updated your account VAT field to IE1234567V and marked future EU B2B invoices as reverse-charged unless you tell us otherwise.
- HubSpot ticket updated: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/quickscale/ticket/QS-2981 — I set the expected closure for 2026-09-14 after our internal verification pass.

If anything in the corrected invoice doesn't match your accounting expectations, flag it and we’ll fix it quickly. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll also follow up with an engineering postmortem on the SDK retry behavior and offer guidance to prevent recurrence.

Best,
Sofia
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
